issue_context.title: daemonset stuck in `Completed` state after a reboot (with graceful kubelet shutdown)
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I can reproduce this reliably with Calico v3.25.0 CNI, installed straight from the upstream [manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/projectcalico/calico/v3.25.0/manifests/calico.yaml).

It seems to be a **regression** in Kubernetes 1.27.0-rc.0 compared to 1.27.0-beta.0, at least I can't reproduce it with beta.0.

Cluster is deployed, and everything is ready & healthy. After a series of node reboots some `calico-node` pods are stuck in `Completed` state and never recover:

```
NAMESPACE       NAME                                                   READY   STATUS      RESTARTS        AGE     IP               NODE                           NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
kube-system     calico-kube-controllers-6c99c8747f-q5g8d               1/1     Running     2 (14m ago)     26m     192.168.62.135   talos-default-controlplane-2   <none>           <none>
kube-system     calico-node-hm7pf                                      1/1     Running     2 (12m ago)     25m     172.20.0.2       talos-default-controlplane-1   <none>           <none>
kube-system     calico-node-hvws2                                      1/1     Running     2 (11m ago)     25m     172.20.0.4       talos-default-controlplane-3   <none>           <none>
kube-system     calico-node-kf69z                                      0/1     Completed   1               25m     172.20.0.6       talos-default-worker-2         <none>           <none>
kube-system     calico-node-lpkxj                                      0/1     Completed   1 (18m ago)     25m     172.20.0.5       talos-default-worker-1         <none>           <none>
kube-system     calico-node-pngj7                                      1/1     Running     2 (14m ago)     26m     172.20.0.3       talos-default-controlplane-2   <none>           <none>
```

This of course disrupts the CNI and affects the scheduled workloads.

The daemonset is "happy" with 2 pods being out:

```
NAMESPACE     NAME          DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   NODE SELECTOR            AGE   CONTAINERS    IMAGES                                    SELECTOR
kube-system   calico-node   5         5         3       5            3           kubernetes.io/os=linux   45m   calico-node   docker.io/calico/node:v3.25.0             k8s-app=calico-node
```

If I delete the `Completed` pod manually, the pod recovers without any issues.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pods are restarted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Bring up a cluster with graceful node shutdown, reboot nodes a few times (including multiple node at anoce).

### Anything else we need to know?

> At the same time I don't quite understand what is exactly wrong, as if I just do a daemonset with `sleep 10` command, the pod also enters `Completed` state, but it gets quickly restarted by the `kubelet` via `CrashLoopBackOff` transition.

This is because of `restartPolicy: Always`. The pod doesn't reach the `Succeeded` phase in this case. The kubelet just recreates the containers. However, when a pod is actually marked as "Succeeded" then kubelet would stop looking at it.

However, it should be the responsibility of the daemonset controller to recreate a pod.

Following the sig-apps advise opened the PR (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117073) with an integration test for DaemonSet. 

It passes for Failed pods, but fails for Succeeded. In other words, the succeeded pods are not restarted. I'm yet to investigate (probably tomorrow) why this is so, but it seems like a bug. In the meanwhile some expertise about DaemonSets would be helpful.

Thanks for reporting this. I suppose this might be related to the fact that `restartAlways` pods (created by daemonset) can now be marked as [terminal phase](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d89d5ab2680bc74fe4487ad71e514f4e0812d9ce/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1463-L1486) in v1.27.

When graceful node shutdown happens, we terminate the pod with `killPodNow`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d89d5ab2680bc74fe4487ad71e514f4e0812d9ce/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L377

which will trigger kubelet to terminate the pod in pod worker (`syncTerminatingPod/syncTerminatedPod`) and eventually I assume set a terminal phase on the pod. We should verify if that is what is happening here.

In either case, +1 on comment that I would expect that daemonset controller should recreate a pod if it is marked completed.

I will note that the intent for graceful shutdown was always that pods could be marked Succeeded (vs just Failed), since the pod is indeed terminal.  It's likely that this was previously racy (no guarantee succeeded made it to the apiserver) and #115331 fixed that.

However, outside of graceful shutdown this should never occur - do we have any evidence a RestartAlways pod went succeeded in that case (wasn't clear from the thread)?  That would be a serious bug.

> However, outside of graceful shutdown this should never occur - do we have any evidence a RestartAlways pod went succeeded in that case (wasn't clear from the thread)? That would be a serious bug.

I think Succeeded would also be possible in other scenarios, like deletion (deletionTimestamp!=nil). This I've tested for Job pods, but I think DS pods would behave the same. 

Except for deletion I think the behavior is limited to graceful node shutdown, which invokes the kill function, but respects the Succeeded phase: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L377-L381. Other uses of the kill function unconditionally set Failed, such as the eviction manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/eviction/eviction_manager.go#L586.

EDIT: oh, actually for Jobs we don't use restartPolicy=Always, but still deleted pods with  restartPolicy=Always may still terminate with Succeeded phase as shown in this test: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d89d5ab2680bc74fe4487ad71e514f4e0812d9ce/test/e2e_node/deleted_pods_test.go#L142
Deletion with RestartAlways is ok, because the pod goes away reasonably fast (but we are adding latency in 1.27 to that path) as you note.
